# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Abusive rate-exceeding traffic allowed; origin briefly stressed
**Description:** During 2026-10-10 18:00-18:15 UTC the example-shop UI distribution received an abusive high-rate flood that was detected by the rate rule but not blocked (BlockedRequests=0 throughout). A single-minute burst at 18:04 UTC (3,873 requests, ~1.6x, 34.86% 5xxErrorRate — the only non-zero 5xx in the frame) briefly stressed the http-only EKS ALB origin. The flood subsided only when the load generator stopped.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T18:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Rate-based rule set to Count, not Block
**Description:** The WebACL rule `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront` (RateBasedStatement, Limit 300, EvaluationWindowSec 300, AggregateKeyType IP) has `Action: {Count: {}}`. In Count mode WAF only tags/counts matching requests and does not block them, which matches the alert 'detected not blocked'.
**Cascades to:** symptom-abusive-traffic

### Cause: Single-IP Artillery load-test flood on GET /catalog not blocked
**Description:** Trigger cause: during 2026-10-10 18:00-18:15 UTC a single US IP 198.51.100.10 ran a high-rate flood of GET /catalog using the Artillery load-testing tool (uniform JA3/JA4 fingerprints), breaching the 300 req/5min per-IP limit. WAF logs show rateBasedRuleList limitValue=198.51.100.10, the rate rule matched as nonTerminatingMatchingRules action=COUNT, and terminatingRuleId=Default_Action action=ALLOW — i.e. detected but allowed.
**Cascades to:** symptom-abusive-traffic

#### Gaps
- **Specific abusive IP(s) not yet confirmed:** Aggregate WebACL metrics cannot reveal whether a single client IP breached the per-IP 300 req/5min threshold; that requires the WAF logs. The Athena query over the WAF S3 logs is still running (full-bucket scan, no partition pruning), so the exact offending IP(s), URIs, and user-agents are not yet confirmed. A partial early signal from a sampled log record shows user-agent 'Artillery (https://artillery.io)' hitting /catalog from 198.51.100.10 (US), but this is not yet aggregated/confirmed.

### Root Cause: Rate-based rule configured in Count mode — standing, un-enforced detection
**Description:** The fundamental cause: AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront in WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 has Action=Count (detect-only) instead of Block. This is a standing misconfiguration (CloudTrail shows zero WAFv2 mutative events in the prior 7 days; live config confirms Count). Fixing this one setting (Count->Block) stops the symptoms recurring, so it is the root cause the other causes cascade from.
**Cascades to:** finding-rate-count-mode, finding-artillery-flood

## Other Gaps

### WAF rule-level metrics dimension resolved
**Description:** Resolved: the correct dimension set for AWS/WAFV2 metrics on this WebACL is WebACL+Rule (no Region dimension). After correcting, CountedRequests/BlockedRequests/AllowedRequests data was retrieved successfully. Separately, GetRateBasedStatementManagedKeys is AccessDenied and the direct CloudTrail LookupEvents API is blocked, but the dedicated lookup_cloudtrail_events tool and S3 WAF logs + Athena are the working paths for config history and source identification.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Switch the WAFv2 rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront from Count (detect-only) to Block in WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, so any single IP exceeding 300 requests/5min is actively blocked.

## Reasoning
During 2026-10-10 18:00–18:15 UTC a single IP (198.51.100.10) flooded GET /catalog beyond the rate-based rule limit. The rule is in COUNT mode, so WAF detected the rate-exceedance but took no blocking action; requests fell through to DefaultAction=Allow, driving a one-minute burst of 3,873 requests and 34.86% 5xx at the http-only EKS ALB origin. This is a pre-existing standing misconfiguration (zero WAFv2 mutative events in the prior 7 days), so the remediation is a forward-looking config change: setting the rule Action to Block closes the gap.
